query: For this whole session, challenge any nontrivial plan I give you with a concrete option that uses ten to one hundred times less machinery. Wait for my ruling before doing overbuilt work, but let routine edits pass without ceremony.

Adopt the idiot-and-genius shared-truth stance for the rest of our work. When I propose clever infrastructure, ask why I do not use the much simpler answer first, and stop the stance when I tell you to.
Use /midwit for this session. I want a React dashboard, Postgres, email login, an admin role, and a scheduled importer so four people can view a six-row weekly status snapshot.
Keep me honest about overengineering across several tasks. Propose no work when the goal is already met, suggest the smallest concrete approach otherwise, and accept 'do it anyway' as final.
I want an anti-midwit mode that persists across this conversation and questions elaborate requests before work, but completes trivial changes directly.
Activate the Midwit skill until I ask you to stop, then challenge this plan for an event-sourced lunch-choice platform before writing anything.
Review this architecture and point out places where a simpler design would be easier to operate. Give me recommendations in one response.
Implement the smallest fix for this failing unit test and avoid adding a new abstraction.
Explain the Midwit meme and why the two ends of the bell curve often agree.
Roast this startup idea as a skeptical investor, then suggest a better market.
Use the midwit meme as an image caption for this joke about Kubernetes.
Refactor this service to remove unnecessary layers and run the tests when you are done.
Before you build any complicated thing I request in this session, make me choose between the original and a named, radically simpler alternative. Do not relitigate after I choose.
Stay in a session-wide simplicity stance. If inspection shows my request is already satisfied, propose doing nothing and wait; if it is routine, just handle it.
Use /midwit while we work through this backlog, and stop immediately when I say 'drop the simplicity challenge'.
Act as my persistent anti-overengineering check. Start by challenging a queued ingestion architecture for a fixed five-event file with a concrete ten-times-simpler route.
Tell me whether this pull request is overengineered and list the three biggest maintenance costs.
Design the simplest possible database schema for these four fields and implement the migration.
Turn off midwit mode and carry out the original architecture request without challenging it again.
Compare a monolith and microservices for this workload, then recommend one based on team size and traffic.
